input.goal: Create a single self-contained index.html: interactive full-viewport HTML5 Canvas orbital particle simulation in dark space (#060913) with central glowing star, orbiting planets with moons and trails, twinkling starfield, glassmorphism HUD, and click-spawned particle bursts.
constraints: Only file is index.html; zero external dependencies (no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts, or URLs); valid JavaScript.

Body/background color #060913; a single <canvas id="sim"> fills the full window, resizes on window resize, and is scaled by window.devicePixelRatio (canvas.width = innerWidth*dpr, ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0)).
Animation loop uses requestAnimationFrame.
Central star drawn with ctx.createRadialGradient, with a subtle corona pulse (radius/alpha oscillating with time).

At least 5 planets with distinct orbital radii, distinct angular speeds and distinct colors; at least 3 moons orbiting planets; each planet has a fading orbital trail (older trail points drawn with lower alpha).
Background starfield of at least 150 stars that twinkle (alpha varies over time per star).
HUD overlay with glassmorphism: semi-transparent background, backdrop-filter: blur(...), border, border-radius.

HUD buttons: <button id="playBtn"> toggles play/pause (text 'Pause' when running, 'Play' when paused); <button id="trailsBtn"> toggles trails (text 'Trails: ON' / 'Trails: OFF'); <button id="resetBtn"> resets simulation time to 0, planet angles to initial, clears trails and burst particles.
Speed slider exactly: <input type="range" id="speed" min="0.2" max="3.0" step="0.1" value="1.0"> with live readout <span id="speedVal"> showing e.g. '1.0x', updated on input event.
Live stats elements: <span id="fps">, <span id="simTime"> (simulation seconds, e.g. '12.3'), <span id="particles"> (active burst particle count), updated at least several times per second.

Clicking the canvas spawns a radial burst of at least 40 glowing particles at the click point, with velocities pointing outward, velocity damping each frame (multiply by factor <1), fade-out by life, and removal when dead.

Expose window.app = {running:boolean, trails:boolean, speed:number, simTime:number, particles:Array (burst particles), planets:Array (length>=5), moons count via app.moonCount:number (>=3), stars:Array (length>=150)} kept live (same object mutated each frame).
Simulation time advances by dt*speed only while running; while paused planets do not move.

content.text:
I've created `index.html` using Tandem, but its automated test run ended with one check still failing: the Reset check.

**What passed:** 39 of the 40 steps in the browser test. These covered:
- the `#060913` background and the full-window canvas scaled for screen density
- 5 planets with different colours, at least 3 moons, and at least 150 twinkling stars
- the animation actually moving
- Play/Pause stopping and restarting the clock
- the Trails toggle
- the speed slider and its readout
- clicking the canvas, which spawns at least 40 burst particles that then fade out and disappear
- the FPS, time and particle-count readouts
- no external files or links

**What failed:** the last check, which pressed Reset, waited 50 ms and expected the simulation time to be under 0.5 s with no particles left. I didn't make any changes after that. The Reset code (`index.html:259`) does set the time to 0 and puts planets, moons, trails and particles back to their starting state. The simulation keeps running after a reset, and the speed was still at 2.5× from an earlier step, so the clock could pass 0.5 s if the test tool took around 200 ms to register the click. That's my best guess at the cause, but I didn't re-run anything to confirm it, so Reset is unverified for now.

I also checked that the JavaScript parses without errors.
